messages:
Jason (ACME): Hey team — since the rollout this morning (v3.12), our chatbot started answering in a really weird way. Prompts that used to return direct instructions are now paraphrased and sometimes drop bullet lists. This started right after 08:15 UTC when we saw the new chat template + tokenizer change. Request IDs: rq_5f9c2a, rq_5f9c2b. Anyone seen this?

Anna Support: sorry you're hitting this, Jason. Can you paste a minimal repro? Also which model variant did you get routed to (we'll check routing logs). If you have an example of before/after outputs that'd help.

Jason (ACME): sure — minimal is below. Before (yesterday) this prompt yielded a numbered list; now it gives a short paragraph and misses steps. I captured two responses.

Jason (ACME): ```
POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat
{
  "model": "redwood-std-1",
  "messages": [
    {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant."},
    {"role": "user", "content": "How do I reset my API key? Provide a 3-step numbered list."}
  ]
}
```

Jason (ACME): BEFORE (2026-03-14):
1) Go to Settings -> API Keys
2) Click rotate
3) Update app config

Jason (ACME): AFTER (2026-03-15 08:20 UTC):
Please go to your account settings and rotate the key. Then update your app with the new key.

Anna Support: thanks, that really helps. I pulled the routing log for rq_5f9c2a: routed to redwood-std-1@pool-7, config shows chat_template=compact_v2, tokenizer=tok-v2. I also see a note in today's deploy: "chat-template: escape-curly update" and "tokenizer: merge-whitespace-fix". @Sam Runtime / @Mei ML can you confirm if any of those changes could alter tokenization of system/user roles?

Sam Runtime: pinged. Looking into deploy logs. The deploy-bot shows: 
```
deploy-bot: deploy v3.12 started 2026-03-15T07:58:31Z
 - service: chat-template
 - service: tokenizer
 - rollout strategy: canary (10%) -> 100%
 - change: chat templates now strip leading newlines; tokenizer now normalizes multi-space sequences
deploy-bot: canary completed 08:05, global rollout 08:12
```

Mei ML: quick thought — the tokenizer normalization removed a leading space that was previously used as a sentinel to separate the system prompt from the user message in the compact_v2 chat template. That sentinel was relied on by the model to preserve a discrete token boundary. Without it, the model sometimes interprets the system and user content as a merged sequence, which can change attention and make list tokens ("1.") less likely.

Mei ML: repro I ran locally: with tok-v1 + compact_v2 system had a leading "\n" and tokenized as: [<sys>, "\n", "You", "are", ...]; with tok-v2 that "\n" collapses and the token sequence is different. Small changes in early tokens caused the LM to prefer a paragraph instead of enumerated bullets.

Anna Support: that's a great root cause candidate. Jason, can you confirm whether you pass any explicit leading whitespace in your system message? If not, as a temporary workaround can you prefix the system content with a single newline or a sentinel like "---" so the tokenizer retains separation?

Jason (ACME): we don't add leading whitespace; our SDK constructs system messages directly. We can try the sentinel workaround. Is there a recommended sentinel?

Mei ML: try adding "\n---\n" at the start of the system message, e.g.:
```
{"role":"system","content":"\n---\nYou are a helpful assistant."}
```
That preserves a stable token boundary across tok-v1 and tok-v2. It restored list outputs in my quick test.

Sam Runtime: operational note — long-term we should avoid relying on whitespace sensitivity. Two remediation paths: 1) roll back tokenizer norm to tok-v1 for the next patch release, or 2) update chat-template compact_v2 to explicitly include a dedicated separator token (e.g., "<|sep|>") that is emitted as a single token by tokenizer and preserved by merges. Both have tradeoffs: rollback reduces perf/consistency gains; separator requires coordinated tokenizer + template release.

Oliver Product: flagging product impact: multiple customers reported similar regressions via support in the past hour. We need a customer comms plan if rollback is needed. @Anna Support collect impacted customers + severity.

Anna Support: working on a list. So far: ACME (high), beta_partner_xyz (med), internal-internal-test (low). I've opened CS-5232 and attached logs.

Anna Support: Jason — can you confirm whether you want us to: A) apply the sentinel patch to your app (we can suggest SDK change), B) route your traffic to legacy tokenizer variant while we fix, or C) wait for a full rollback?

Jason (ACME): please route us to legacy variant for now, that minimizes risk for our customers. We can also apply sentinel as a second line.

Sam Runtime: done — routing change submitted, request id route-change-9876. I'll confirm once the traffic shift completes and run a quick smoke test.

deploy-bot: route-change-9876 applied to customer ACME at 2026-03-15T09:02:11Z (status: partial, 20% -> 100% over 3m).

Sam Runtime: smoke test results: pre-change sample produced paragraph; after routing to tok-v1 it returns an enumerated list again. Verified on rq_5f9c2a replica.

Mei ML: next steps for engineering:
 - create small guard in chat-template to always inject explicit separator token (PR in progress: https://git.internal/pr/4421)
 - add tokenizer regression tests that include role-separation cases and list preservation metrics
 - consider a canary that runs a subset of requests through tok-v2 + tok-v1 and compares output shape before rolling out

Sam Runtime: I'll prioritize a short rollback patch if necessary; otherwise we'll coordinate template+tokenizer follow-up and a controlled re-rollout.

Anna Support: I'll update ACME and other customers (CS-5232) with the routing workaround and ETA for a long-term fix. Thanks @Mei ML and @Sam Runtime for the quick diagnosis. :thumbsup:

Jason (ACME): thanks everyone — the routing fix restored expected outputs. Please keep us posted on the permanent fix and any SDK changes we should make.

Mei ML: noted. I'll add a note in the release changelog about tokenizer/template coupling and a sample SDK snippet for the sentinel workaround.

Anna Support: closing the support loop for now; will reopen if we see reoccurrence.

Sam Runtime: leaving a follow-up action: "ENG-894: ensure tokenizer/template compatibility tests" assigned to eng-ml.

deploy-bot: incident-log appended: incident-2026-03-15-tokenizer-regression, severity: P2, status: monitoring.
